STUDY SESSION:

1.  STUDY SESSION: EXTERIOR COLORS OF RESIDENTIAL AND NON-
  RESIDENTIAL BUILDINGS

  Planning Director Forbes presented regulations for exterior colors of residential
  and non-residential buildings, stating regulation is challenging because colors are
  subjective and personal; color shade appearance adjusts on various mediums;
  light and shadows affect the appearance; and lastly each Homeowner Association
  (HOA) has their own approved color palettes.

  Mr. Forbes reviewed the Westlake Village Municipal Code Design Standards and
  Zoning Clearance requirements, stating the interpretation of the earthtone color
  palette has varied over the years. Mr. Forbes presented a series of color samples
  to guide the City Council discussion on color hues and shades. The Light
  Reflective Value (LRV) and how LRV could be used to objectively regulate
  acceptable shades of paint was presented. The LRV is a number scale from zero
  to 100 that quantifies the amount of light a given color reflects. The greater the
  amount of light reflected, the lighter the color appears and the higher the LRV. An
  LRV of zero is pure black, while an LRV of 100 is pure white. All paint
  manufacturers provide LRV values for each of their paint colors, providing an
  objective and uniform means of regulating the shade of all brands and types of
  paint.

  Planning Director Forbes noted that staff reviewed hundreds of colors and is
  recommending an acceptable LRV range of 22 (considered a medium dark shade)
  to 79 (considered an off-white shade), that apply to the main building color and not
  apply to roofs, accents, trim, or fa9ade materials such as stone and brick.

  City Council discussion was to address the eight questions posed by Staff, which
  provided direction to staff on how to proceed with developing guidelines. City
  Council determined that Guidelines not regulations would be developed, and that
  HOA's would play a more critical role in the color approval process.
